To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Mn(VII)-based oxidation of phenolics is significantly enhanced by the presence of ligand stabilizing agents, and the enhancement effects can be attributed to the stabilization of in situ formed manganese intermediates.

(1) Mn(VII) can oxidize phenolics, including triclosan at pH values of ∼5-9, (2) Mn(VII)-mediated oxidation of phenolics in the presence of stabilizing ligands (e.g., phosphate, pyrophosphate, and humic substances) is enhanced, and (3) the enhancement is due to the formation of highly active Mn(INT)(aq).

Mn(VII) is a promising oxidant for the degradation of phenolic compounds, especially when the presence of ligand stabilizers is considered, and that the catalytic role played by MnO(2)/MnO(2) and Mn(INT)(aq)/Mn(INT)(s) colloids is important in the oxidation processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the complex Mn(VII) redox chemistry in aqueous solution, which is of fundamental importance in environmental remediation and water purification.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidation enhancement of Mn(VII)-triclosan reaction by ligands and natural matrices is due to the formation and stabilization of aqueous manganese intermediated (Mn(INT)) in situ.

the Mn(VII) reaction is highly sensitive to ligand and background matrix effects, and the in situ formed Mn(III/IV) intermediates play an important role in the Mn(VII)-mediated oxidation of phenolics.
Mn(VII) is capable of oxidizing phenolics in natural water and wastewaters, but the oxidation rate is significantly affected by the presence of various inorganic ligands and natural organic matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Mn(VII) could serve as a promising oxidant in water remediation for a wide pH range, and that the addition of ligands and natural organic matter (NOM) would be beneficial for Mn(VII) to achieve a more efficient oxidation of phenolics in natural waters.

the oxidation enhancement of Mn(VII)-mediated oxidation of phenolic derivatives is attributed to the catalytic role played by the in situ formed Mn(INT)(aq), as well as the stabilizing effects of ligands and background matrices.
ligand-promoted Mn(VII) catalyzed oxidations of phenolic pollutants are of great importance in natural and engineered systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ligands, in situ formed Mn(II) and Mn(III) species, MnO(2), and background organic matter all contribute to the oxidation of phenolic pollutants by Mn(VII).

Mn(VII) can be used as a promising oxidant for the oxidative removal and degradation of phenolic compounds in water, and that the presence of stabilizing ligands in water can significantly enhance the reactivity of Mn(VII), which might be useful in the design of new Mn(VII)-based water treatment processes for the oxidative removal/detoxification of recalcitrant organic contaminants in water.

Mn(VII) is an excellent oxidant for phenolic pollutants in the environment, and that the oxidation efficiency can be further improved by the presence of stabilizing agents and in situ formed Mn oxides.
